notes: 2026-08-02 pass: Phaladeepika (Adhyayas V-VIII, XIX) and Aiyar's Brhajjataka translation were both searched broadly for worked-example markers (explicit birth data plus a stated verdict). Neither turned one up; both are rule catalogs, not worked-example collections, in the chapters inspected. That is itself a finding, not a gap glossed over - see the two updated inventory entries below. The BPHS 1899 witness was fetched to a local mirror and its OCR is confirmed (not merely suspected) unusable: of the full text, effectively none of the Devanagari/Hindi survived OCR as anything but literal '?' characters. A THIRD Saravali witness (Nirnaya Sagar Press, 1907, CC0) was located and is, for the first time in this corpus, legible Devanagari rather than corrupted OCR - it has not yet been read for content and is recorded as the next task, not as a worked-example find. No customer-facing chart is encoded anywhere in this file; extracted delineation RULES (as opposed to worked EXAMPLES) from Phaladeepika now live in delineation_rule_manifest.json, which is a separate document from this worked-example suite. 2026-08-05: three arithmetic suites added from the BPHS Subodhini 1899 own worked computations (sadbala of the Sun, ashtakavarga pinda of the Sun, and the eight bhinnashtakavarga row-sums). These are a different KIND of worked example from a judged nativity: the author is working his own arithmetic rather than judging a native, so there is no interpretive verdict to agree or disagree with - but there is also no translation judgment to dispute, and the engine either reproduces the printed number or it does not. Requirement 4 of the defensibility standard asks for the tradition own worked examples; these are the first in this tradition that are mechanically checkable end to end.

examples.description: The chapters most likely to carry a worked chart in a classical delineation manual - the yoga catalog (V-VII), the planet-in-bhava chapter (VIII), and the dasha-results chapter (XIX) - were read directly, not sampled by keyword search alone, since a worked chart's numbers would not keyword-match. Adhyayas XI-XII (women's horoscope, children) were located but deliberately not mined for rules, since their subject matter (progeny counts, fertility) falls under this tradition's own safety limits on fertility/health claims.

claims.author_states: Adhyayas V-VIII and XIX are entirely rule catalogs: named-yoga definitions and results (Pancha Mahapurusha, Kesari/Sakata, Mahabhagya, Adhama/Sama/Varishtha, Sunapha/Anapha/Durudhara/Kemadruma, Vesi/Vaasi/Kartari, the '4 Rajayogas', Neechabhanga Rajayoga), planet-in-bhava results for 12 houses across 8 of 9 grahas (Sun recovered for 5 of 12 houses only), and Vimshottari mahadasha significations for all 9 grahas - all now extracted into jyotisha/delineation_rule_manifest.json. None of these chapters presents a nativity with real or stated birth data, computed positions, and an author-given overall verdict of the kind Sloka-by-sloka rule catalogs do not provide. This is a negative finding about these specific chapters, not a claim that Phaladeepika as a whole contains no worked chart anywhere (Adhyayas IX-XVIII, XX-XXVIII were not inspected in this pass).

blockers: Adhyayas IX-XVIII (rasi-as-lagna effects, kalatra bhava, women's horoscope, issue, longevity, death, rasi general effects, exit-from-the-world, planetary conjunctions) and XX-XXVIII (dasha subdivisions, Kalachakra dasha, Ashtakavarga, upagrahas, transits, miscellanea) were not inspected in this pass and could still contain a worked chart.

Delineation rules extracted from the chapters that WERE inspected are in jyotisha/delineation_rule_manifest.json, not in this file - this entry records only the worked-example search, which came back negative.

examples.location: BPHS varga chapters; the rule is stated identically across the standard texts
examples.description: The classical navamsha rule states that movable signs begin their D9 from themselves, fixed signs from the ninth sign, and dual signs from the fifth. Those three statements have mechanically checkable consequences, verified here without needing a worked chart: the division counts must balance and the three starting rules must hold exactly.

claims.author_states: The 108 navamsha divisions distribute across the twelve signs exactly nine times each.
A movable sign begins its navamsha series from itself: the first navamsha of Aries is Aries.
A fixed sign begins from the ninth sign: the first navamsha of Taurus is Capricorn.
A dual sign begins from the fifth sign: the first navamsha of Gemini is Libra.
The series closes: the final navamsha of Pisces is Pisces.

examples.location: Uttara-khanda adhyaya 2, commentary on slokas 8-32, pages 42-60 of the 1899 printing
examples.description: The chapter does not merely state the sadbala formulas - it computes them for one specific chart and prints every intermediate. This is the first material in the Jyotisha pack that can be checked without any translation judgment at all: the numbers either come out or they do not. All of the following were recomputed from the printed inputs on 2026-08-04 and reproduce the printed outputs exactly. Unit throughout: rupa, virupa, sixtieth - one rupa being sixty virupas.

claims.author_states: Sun at 10|4|14, debilitation at 6|10; arc 3|24|14 = 114 deg 14 min; divided by three, uccha-bala 38|04 virupas
arc 147 deg 05 min divided by three gives the Sun dig-bala 0|49|01
ishta 8|16, half-day 13|54; nata 5|38, unnata 24|22; doubled 48|44 is the day-strength of the Sun, Venus and Jupiter, and 60 less that, 11|16, is that of the Moon, Mars and Saturn
Moon 8|25|29 less Sun 10|4|14 gives 10|21|15; from the circle 1|8|45 = 38 deg 45 min; divided by three, 12|55 for the benefics, and 60 less that, 47|05, for the Sun
natonnata 0|48|44 plus paksha 0|47|5 plus day-and-night 1|0|0 plus the year-lord group 0|30|0 is the Sun kala-bala, 3|5|49
claims.note: recomputed 2026-08-04: the four terms sum exactly

claims.author_states: sayana Sun 10|26|15, bhuja 1|3|45; after the khandas 45, 33, 12 and subtraction from three rasis, 1|10|52|30 = 40 deg 52 min 30 sec; divided by three 13|37|30; doubled for the Sun, 27|15

sthana 4|18|4, dig 0|49|1, kala 3|5|49, cheshta 0|27|15, naisargika 1|0|0; their sum 9|40|9; the benefic aspect on the Sun being 0|4|22 in surplus, a quarter of it 0|1|5 is added, giving the Sun sadbala 9|41|14
claims.note: THE central check. Recomputed 2026-08-04: the five components sum to 9.66917 rupas = 9|40|9, and the quarter-drsti correction gives 9|41|14. Both printed figures reproduce exactly.

claims.author_states: the first bhava lord Mars has sadbala 5|59|16; a quarter of the net benefic aspect on the bhava, 0|6|52, is added, giving 6|6|8; the aspect of Mercury and Jupiter 0|50|41 is added, giving the bhava-bala 6|56|49; its dig-bala, 85 deg 15 min divided by three = 28|25, brings it to 7|25|14

the five component minima 165, 35, 50, 112, 30 for Jupiter, Mercury and the Sun; 133, 50, 30, 100, 40 for Venus and the Moon; 96, 30, 40, 67, 20 for Mars and Saturn; their sums being the panchabala-samhati 6|32, 5|53 and 4|13 rupas
